 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the MV Act challenging the impugned judgment and award dated 17.1.2018 passed in MVC No.1520/2016 by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Challakere.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal, Challakere
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act claiming just and proper compensation having sustained injuries in a road traffic accident occurred on 21.11.2014 claiming just and proper compensation.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,36,000/- with interest at 9% p.a.
Being satisfied, the appellant is in appeal for enhancement of compensation.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondent - Insurance Company.
The claimant having sustained the accidental injuries on 21.11.2014 was aged about 11 years as on the date of accident, is not disputed.

As per Ex.P7 - wound certificate and Ex.P8 - OPD record, the claimant sustained lacerated wound over right foot upto bone depth, and the injury is grievous in Sri. B Balaji vs Ramanjineyalu P on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55976093/

sentences.text: The doctor, who was examined as PW2, opined that Ex.P10 - disability certificate indicating that the petitioner sustained 30% disability to his right leg, and the functional disability at 13%.

5. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Master Mallikarjun -vs- Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Limited and another - AIR 2014 SC 736 has held that if the disability is above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs would be appropriate compensation.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun -vs- Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Limited and another - AIR 2014 SC 736
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the functional disability of the claimant has been assessed at 13%.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled for a sum of Rs.3 lakh towards loss of amenities.

The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.22,000/- towards medical expenses, however, upon perusal of the medical bills at Exs.P13 - 144,
the claimant has spent a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards medical expenses.
The compensation amount of Rs.12,000/- awarded under the head of attendant expenses is just and proper.

Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal requires to be reassessed as follows:
1) Loss of amenities = Rs.3,00,000/-
2) Medical expenses = Rs.40,000/-
3) Attendent expenses = Rs.12,000/-
The appeal is allowed in part.
6. In all, the appellant/claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.3,52,000/- in addition to Rs.1,36,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced compensation of Rs.2,16,000/- shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till actual realization.
To this extent, the award passed by the Tribunal stands modified.
7. The enhanced amount to be deposited by the respondent - Insurance Company within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
